title: Refactor RAG example to use template retriever interface + standardized errors
author: Sabrina James
release_notes:
- RAG example now uses the same Retriever abstraction as the Quickstart templates
- Standardized error taxonomy + user-facing messages for common retrieval failures
- Added basic instrumentation hooks (spans + log fields) consistent with template conventions
description:
## Summary
This refactors the existing RAG example to align with the new Quickstart template retriever abstraction and error handling patterns. Goal is to keep examples and templates consistent so users don’t learn one-off patterns from the examples.

Key changes:
- Introduce `Retriever` interface usage in the example (mirrors template `retriever` contract)
- Replace ad-hoc exceptions with standardized error types + taxonomy mapping
- Normalize “empty retrieval” behavior (don’t silently answer without sources unless explicitly configured)
- Add minimal tracing/log conventions (request id passthrough + span names) so troubleshooting matches docs

## Motivation / Context
Templates are shipping a shared retriever interface + error taxonomy. The current RAG example has:
- Tight coupling to a specific vector store implementation
- Inconsistent failure modes (empty results returns 200 with hallucinated answer)
- Non-standard logging and no correlation id propagation

This PR updates the example so it stays in lockstep with template conventions.

## Design notes
### Retriever contract
The example now depends on a small interface:
- `retrieve(query, *, top_k, filters) -> List[RetrievedChunk]`
- `RetrievedChunk` includes `text`, `source_id`, `score`, and optional `metadata`

Vector store specifics live behind an adapter.

### Error handling
The example now uses a template-style taxonomy:
- `RetrievalConfigError` (misconfiguration / missing index)
- `RetrievalTimeoutError`
- `RetrievalEmptyResultError`
- `RetrievalBackendError` (unexpected vector store failure)

User-facing behavior:
- Empty retrieval returns a structured error by default with a “how to fix” hint
- Optional `ALLOW_EMPTY_RETRIEVAL=true` keeps prior behavior for folks demoing quickly

### Observability
Adds:
- Span `rag.retrieve` with attributes: `rag.top_k`, `rag.filter_applied` (boolean), `rag.result_count`
- Log fields: `redwood.request_id` (if present), `rag.query_hash` (no raw query)

## Implementation
Commits:
- `c1a0d7b` examples/rag: add retriever interface adapter scaffolding
- `5e3b2c1` examples/rag: switch query path to use retriever + chunk normalization
- `df2129e` examples/rag: add standardized errors + empty result behavior
- `aa8bd41` examples/rag: add basic tracing/log fields and redaction guard
- `b4a81f3` docs: update README and troubleshooting section

Changed areas (high-level):
- `examples/rag/`:
  - `retriever.py` / `retriever.ts` adapter wiring (depending on example flavor)
  - `rag_pipeline.*` updated to call `retriever.retrieve(...)`
  - error mapping + user-facing messages
- `examples/rag/README.md` updated to match template language and troubleshooting

Illustrative snippet (Python):

Old:
- Call vector store client directly in pipeline; empty results fall through.

New:
- `chunks = retriever.retrieve(query, top_k=top_k, filters=filters)`
- `if not chunks and not allow_empty: raise RetrievalEmptyResultError("No relevant chunks found", hint="Run ingest step or verify INDEX_PATH")`

## Test plan
- `make lint` / `make typecheck`
- `pytest -k rag` (covers empty retrieval + backend error mapping)
- Manual:
  - Run ingest
  - Query known doc
  - Query nonsense string (validate empty retrieval error)

## Screenshots / Output
- Included updated terminal output in README showing empty retrieval error text and remediation.

## Follow-ups
- Once templates land TS retriever adapters, we should port the TS example fully to the shared package instead of duplicating helper types here.

Refs:
- Linear: ENG-4182 (RAG+agent template), ENG-4187 (config schema/validation)
- Related: redwood-quickstarts PR-105 (retriever interface + adapters)
review_conversation:
Monica Patel (review): This looks aligned with the template contract. Two asks: (1) please ensure we never log raw user queries; (2) can we make empty retrieval behavior explicit in README so users don’t think it’s a model failure.

Sabrina James (author): Good call. I swapped raw query logging to `rag.query_hash` and added a note in README under Troubleshooting + an env var section for `ALLOW_EMPTY_RETRIEVAL`.

Allison Grant (review): For spans, `rag.result_count` is fine, but please avoid any per-document IDs as span attributes (cardinality). Also, can you rename span to `rag.retrieval` to match convention used in the templates?

Sabrina James (author): Updated: span is now `rag.retrieval`, removed `source_id` attribute entirely, and kept only booleans + counts.

Wei Chen (review): README wording: can we match the docs phrasing (“retrieval returned 0 chunks”) and link to the ingest step earlier? Also add a short section on what to do when `INDEX_PATH` is missing.

Sabrina James (author): Updated README to match phrasing and moved ingest instructions up. Added a dedicated troubleshooting bullet for missing index.

Monica Patel (approval): LGTM after latest push. Thanks for keeping behavior compatible via the env flag.

Allison Grant (approval): Approved. Attributes look safe now.

Wei Chen (approval): Approved.
